approach: Differentiate v to check whether the acceleration is constant, then integrate v for the displacement.

steps.text: Differentiate v with respect to time to get the acceleration.
The acceleration is constant in magnitude and direction for every t, even though v itself changes direction with time.
Integrate v with respect to time from 0 to 1 s to get the displacement.
Since the acceleration is constant, v = u + at can be applied; checking it at t = 1 s confirms this matches v(1).
steps.equation: u + at = 2î + 2ĵ = v(1), so yes, v = u + at applies

final_answer.value: a = 2ĵ m/s²; displacement = (2î + ĵ) m; yes, v = u + at can be applied because a is constant

common_mistakes.text: Assuming v = u + at cannot be applied because the velocity's direction changes with time, without checking whether the acceleration itself is constant.
